name: Operating Systems
description: How an operating system manages a machine: processes and threads, scheduling, synchronisation, memory and virtual memory, file systems, and input/output.

topics.name: Operating System Structure
topics.summary: What an OS is for, and the boundary it maintains between programs and hardware.

subtopics.name: The Role of an Operating System

objectives.text: State the principal responsibilities of an operating system
Explain the abstraction an OS provides over raw hardware
Distinguish monolithic, microkernel and layered designs

subtopics.name: System Calls and Privilege
subtopics.summary: User and kernel mode, traps, and the system call interface.

objectives.text: Explain the transition from user mode to kernel mode during a system call
Describe why privilege separation is required for protection
Trace the steps of a read system call

subtopics.name: Interrupts and Exceptions
subtopics.summary: Hardware interrupts, exceptions and the handler mechanism.

objectives.text: Distinguish an interrupt from an exception and from a system call
Describe the actions taken when an interrupt arrives
Explain why interrupt handlers must be short

topics.name: Processes and Threads
topics.summary: The unit of execution, its state, and how the OS switches between many of them.

subtopics.name: The Process Model
subtopics.summary: Address space, process control block, process states and lifecycle.

objectives.text: Describe the contents of a process control block
Draw the process state diagram and the transitions between states
Explain what happens during process creation and termination

subtopics.name: Threads
subtopics.summary: Multiple execution contexts sharing an address space, and user versus kernel threads.

objectives.text: Compare a thread with a process in terms of what is shared
State the advantages and risks of multithreading
Distinguish user-level from kernel-level threads

subtopics.name: Context Switching
subtopics.summary: Saving and restoring execution state, and the cost of doing so.

objectives.text: List the state saved and restored during a context switch
Explain why context switching has a measurable cost
Compare the cost of a thread switch with a process switch

topics.name: CPU Scheduling
topics.summary: Deciding which runnable process runs next, and what that decision optimises.

subtopics.name: Scheduling Criteria
subtopics.summary: Throughput, turnaround, waiting and response time, and the trade-offs between them.

objectives.text: Define throughput, turnaround time, waiting time and response time
Explain why optimising one criterion can degrade another
Distinguish preemptive from non-preemptive scheduling

subtopics.name: Scheduling Algorithms
subtopics.summary: FCFS, SJF, round robin, priority scheduling and multilevel feedback queues.

objectives.text: Compute average waiting and turnaround time for a given schedule
Compare round robin and shortest-job-first on a workload
Explain starvation and how ageing addresses it

subtopics.name: Real-Time and Multiprocessor Scheduling
subtopics.summary: Deadlines, rate-monotonic scheduling and scheduling across cores.

objectives.text: Distinguish hard from soft real-time requirements
Explain the principle of rate-monotonic scheduling
Describe load balancing and processor affinity on a multicore system

topics.name: Concurrency and Synchronisation
topics.summary: Coordinating threads that share data — the source of the hardest bugs in systems programming.

subtopics.name: Race Conditions and Critical Sections
subtopics.summary: Interleaving, the critical section problem and its requirements.

objectives.text: Identify a race condition in an interleaved execution
State the mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting requirements
Explain why an increment operation is not atomic

subtopics.name: Locks, Semaphores and Monitors
subtopics.summary: Mutual exclusion primitives and condition variables.

objectives.text: Use a mutex to protect a critical section correctly
Solve a producer-consumer problem with semaphores
Explain the role of a condition variable in a monitor

subtopics.name: Deadlock
subtopics.summary: The four necessary conditions, and prevention, avoidance and detection.

objectives.text: State the four necessary conditions for deadlock
Detect a deadlock from a resource allocation graph
Compare deadlock prevention, avoidance and detection strategies

topics.name: Memory Management
topics.summary: Giving every process the illusion of a large private address space.

subtopics.name: Memory Allocation
subtopics.summary: Contiguous allocation, fragmentation and allocation strategies.

objectives.text: Distinguish internal from external fragmentation
Apply first-fit, best-fit and worst-fit to an allocation request
Explain why compaction is expensive

subtopics.name: Paging and Address Translation
subtopics.summary: Pages, frames, page tables and the translation lookaside buffer.

objectives.text: Translate a virtual address to a physical address using a page table
Explain the purpose of the TLB and the cost of a TLB miss
Describe multi-level page tables and why they are used

subtopics.name: Virtual Memory and Replacement
subtopics.summary: Demand paging, page faults, replacement policies and thrashing.

objectives.text: Describe the sequence of events on a page fault
Apply FIFO, LRU and optimal replacement to a reference string and count faults
Explain thrashing and how the working set model addresses it

topics.name: File Systems and I/O
topics.summary: Persistent storage, its organisation, and how the OS drives devices.

subtopics.name: File System Structure
subtopics.summary: Files, directories, inodes and allocation methods.

objectives.text: Describe how an inode locates the blocks of a file
Compare contiguous, linked and indexed allocation
Explain how a directory maps a name to a file

subtopics.name: Reliability and Journalling
subtopics.summary: Crash consistency, journalling and caching of file system data.

objectives.text: Explain how a crash mid-write can corrupt a file system
Describe how journalling restores consistency after a crash
State the trade-off between write caching and durability

subtopics.name: I/O Systems
subtopics.summary: Device drivers, polling, interrupts and direct memory access.

objectives.text: Compare polling with interrupt-driven I/O
Explain the role of DMA in reducing CPU involvement
Describe the function of a device driver in the I/O stack
